spans.s: unmāna (IE 8-6; EI 15, 21, 29), name of a small land measure; same as udāna or udamāna (q. v.).

unmara (EI 30), Sanskritised form of Prakrit ummara (cf. umbara); threshold. Merchants, who were often absent from home for a long time, were sometimes made free from unmara-bheda (entry into their house) by royal officers probably because they paid their dues on their return from business tours. Cf. prātibhedikā.
